subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & deployment mode — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Lily Zhang <lily.zhang@mediagen.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap: deployment mode options + sizing worksheet attached

Hi Lily — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking us through Mediagen's production goals. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Peak inference traffic target: ~120 TPS sustained with bursts to 220 TPS for short windows
- Typical request token mix: 80% short prompts (~30 tokens in, ~80 tokens out), 20% long prompts (up to 2k input / 1k output)
- Latency target: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for short prompts
- Data posture: customer PII in payloads, SOC2 + occasional external audits; prefer isolated tenancy for production
- Preferred timeline: pilot in 4–6 weeks, production rollout by end of Q2

Deployment mode considerations we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to start, lower operational lift, shared tenancy (acceptable for evaluation but not ideal for regulated data)
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in a customer-only cluster (recommended if you want predictable costs and isolation without managing infra)
- Private VPC / on-prem: full control, necessary only if required by procurement/compliance (we should confirm your auditors' stance)

Attached: mediagen-dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx — please fill in any missing historic qps, token-length distribution, expected concurrency per worker, and retention/compliance constraints.

Ask / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the 120 TPS sustained / 220 TPS burst numbers and typical token mix if anything above is off?
2) Would your security team accept a Dedicated deployment in a VPC (customer-managed networking) or do they require an on-prem installation?
3) Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sizing call this Thursday to go through the attached worksheet and trade-offs between A100-80GB vs H100 and quantized instances — Monica & Neha will join. Please share 2 time slots that work.

Thanks — we'll prepare an initial cost/throughput sketch after we get the completed worksheet.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) TPS numbers are our target for Phase 1 of the rollout: 120 TPS sustained is correct. Bursts to 220 TPS happen for ~5–10 minute windows after batch jobs (about twice/day).
2) Token mix: your breakdown is accurate — roughly 80/20 short/long. For long prompts, many are inference-heavy (summarization + entity extraction) and we care about consistent p95 latency.
3) Security: our compliance team prefers dedicated tenancy inside our VPC (customer-managed networking) for production — we would consider private on-prem only if auditors demand no external cloud connectivity. Can you confirm whether Dedicated in a customer VPC satisfies most auditors?
4) Regarding GPUs: we don't have a strict preference but want guidance on cost vs latency. Also curious if quantization (4-bit) would materially change hardware needs given the long-prompt use cases.

We'll fill the sizing sheet and return it before Thursday. We can do a call Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT or 16:00–16:30 PT.

Thanks,
Lily

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode options + sizing worksheet attached

Thanks Lily — perfect. A couple of quick answers before the call and a short recommendation based on the numbers you shared: 

Audit/compliance: Dedicated capacity deployed inside your VPC satisfies the vast majority of enterprise auditors we’ve seen. It provides customer-managed networking, KMS integration for keys, and audit log exports. On-prem is only required in very narrow regulated cases. We'll prepare a short compliance note for your auditors.

GPU guidance (summary):
- Short prompts (low-latency): H100 80GB typically gives the best p95 latency and throughput for modern LLMs, especially for batch sizes >1 and models with longer KV cache usage.
- Long-prompt workloads: A100 80GB can be more cost-efficient for very long sequences because of memory bandwidth characteristics; for quantized 4-bit inference (if we accept a small quality delta) you can often use lower-cost instance profiles and still meet p95 targets.
- If you need both predictable low p95 for short prompts and efficient long-prompt handling, a mixed pool (H100 front-line for low-latency, A100-backed workers for long jobs) is a common pattern.

Throughput / concurrency rule-of-thumb (to prepare for Thursday):
- Start with worker footprint assumptions (per-GPU): H100 ~ 14–18 short-prompt TPS (single-stream low-latency), A100 ~ 10–14 depending on model variant and quantization.
- With batching + KV-caching optimizations, effective tokens/second increases; we'll test in pilot to tune batch windows so p95 stays under 250ms for short prompts.

Attached: updated estimate that maps the 120/220 TPS targets to two sizing options (H100-heavy vs mixed pool) — see 20260206-mediagen-dedicated-estimate.pdf. We'll review line-by-line on the call.

Confirming the Thursday slot: 10:00–10:30 PT works for us (I'll send a calendar invite). Monica & Neha will bring a technical runbook and test plan.

See you Thursday — and thanks for filling the sheet.

Best,
Aditya

Lily — quick technical notes ahead of the sizing call: 

1) Concurrency and batching: For short prompts we target concurrency=4–6 per model worker and batching windows of 15–40ms. That keeps p50 very low and keeps tail latency acceptable. For long prompts, we run separate worker pools with higher sequence-length tradeoffs and allow larger batch windows (100–300ms) to get throughput without blowing memory.
2) KV Cache: For chat/interactive flows we recommend enabling prefix caching and sticky routing for known sessions to avoid cold-cache costs. This reduces token compute on repeated conversations considerably.
3) Quantization: 4-bit (GPTQ-style) generally reduces memory and can double per-GPU TPS for short prompts, but quality varies by model. We'll include a quantization-profile run in the pilot to compare outputs on your eval set.
4) Throughput testing: plan for a 48hr soak test during pilot to validate burst behavior to 220 TPS and to capture p95 distribution across time windows and model variants.

I'll bring the raw perf numbers for H100/A100 to the call and a simple test harness you can run in your VPC.

-Monica
